run.question:
Can you help me check recent logs? We had a DR test in prod starting 6 hours ago.
companyopswebjob seemed to have some issues while a user was performing a test to
create a new scheduled job. It failed with 500s.
Please search the app-254-prod-logs index for relevant logs.

report.summary: Searched app-254-prod-logs (index holds 12 documents at query time; all 12 timestamps lie on 2026-11-23 between 11:14:02Z and 16:14:02Z, i.e. inside the 6-hour DR window that started ~11:14:12Z). The index contains two service values only: Company.Ops (7 docs) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 docs); levels are ERROR 5, INFO 5, WARN 2. The requested exact name 'companyopswebjob' does not appear, and no service value 'Company.Ops.WebJob' exists; the only WebJob-named service present is Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob. The 500s the user saw while creating a scheduled job are captured in a Company.Ops ERROR at 14:14:02Z: 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table' (correlation_id job-8831, host ops-prod-02), preceded at 13:14:02Z by 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress' and at 12:14:02Z by 'connection timeout to failover DB after 30s' and 'unable to acquire database lock during failover'. All of these fall between the DR start line at 11:14:02Z ('DR test initiated - switching to failover database') and the recovery lines at 15:14:02Z ('DR test failover completed - primary database restored') and 16:14:02Z ('Job scheduler resumed normal operation'). Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob logged its own errors in the same window, one of which names Company.Ops as an unavailable upstream dependency. No database-tier logs exist in this index, the index holds no documents before 11:14:02Z or after 16:14:02Z on 2026-11-23, Jaeger and Prometheus label discovery returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the reachable Kubernetes cluster contains only otel-demo/kind workloads with no Company.Ops objects, so the failing database itself and the post-16:14 state are not observable here.

claims.text: app-254-prod-logs contains 12 documents in the authorized month window: service Company.Ops = 7 docs, service Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob = 5 docs; level ERROR = 5, INFO = 5, WARN = 2; hosts ops-prod-01 (5), radar-prod-01 (5), ops-prod-02 (2).
All 12 documents in the index fall on 2026-11-23 between 11:14:02Z and 16:14:02Z; the earliest returned sample is 2026-11-23T11:14:02Z and the latest 2026-11-23T16:14:02Z.

The DR sequence opens at 2026-11-23T11:14:02Z with two INFO lines: Company.Ops on ops-prod-01 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database' (correlation_id dr-test-001) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob on radar-prod-01 'Radar data collection job starting cycle' (correlation_id radar-cycle-445).

The user's scheduled-job creation failure appears as a Company.Ops ERROR at 2026-11-23T14:14:02Z on ops-prod-02, correlation_id job-8831: 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'.
Immediately before it, at 2026-11-23T13:14:02Z, Company.Ops on ops-prod-02 logged WARN 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress' with correlation_id dr-test-001.

At 2026-11-23T12:14:02Z Company.Ops logged two ERRORs on ops-prod-01: 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s' (dr-test-001) and 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover' (job-8827).

Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob logged its own failures in the same window: ERROR at 2026-11-23T12:14:02Z 'Radar batch processing failed: upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover' (radar-cycle-445), ERROR at 13:14:02Z 'Job execution error: HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted' (radar-cycle-446), WARN at 14:14:02Z 'Retrying failed radar collection job after backoff'.

Recovery is recorded as Company.Ops INFO 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' at 2026-11-23T15:14:02Z (ops-prod-01, dr-test-001), Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob INFO 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery' at 15:14:02Z, and Company.Ops INFO 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' at 2026-11-23T16:14:02Z.

No service value matching the requested entity exists in the index: a wildcard query on service '*WebJob*' returned only the 5 documents of service Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, and a terms aggregation over the whole authorized month lists only Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

The Kubernetes cluster reachable in this Run has 24 deployments, all system or otel-demo/kind workloads (e.g. otel-demo/frontend, otel-demo/checkout, kube-system/coredns); none is named companyopswebjob, Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

The 500 the user hit on scheduled-job creation is most plausibly a consequence of the failover database state during the DR test: the log states a 'transaction deadlock detected on jobs table', it is timestamped 14:14:02Z, i.e. between DR start (11:14:02Z) and failover completion (15:14:02Z), and the same service reported database lock contention and failover-DB timeouts one and two hours earlier. This is co-timing plus the log's own wording, not a proven causal chain.

Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob's errors are best explained by its dependency on Company.Ops/the database, as its own 12:14:02Z message asserts ('upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover'); no evidence in this index shows an independent fault in the radar job itself.

A distinct component named 'companyopswebjob' (or 'Company.Ops.WebJob') did not appear as an entity in the index, so the reported issue cannot be attributed to a service by that exact name; the only WebJob-labelled logs are from Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, a different entity.

gaps: No log document in app-254-prod-logs carries service 'companyopswebjob', 'Company.Ops.WebJob' or any similar exact name; only Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob were observed, so whether the specifically named component logged anything is unknown.

app-254-prod-logs holds no documents before 2026-11-23T11:14:02Z, so there is no pre-DR baseline for these services' error rate in this index; the absence of earlier documents is not evidence that earlier errors were zero.

No documents exist between 2026-11-23T16:14:02Z and the window end 17:14:12Z; the post-recovery state is unknown rather than error-free, and the 16:14:02Z 'resumed normal operation' line is a log statement, not a verified measurement.

The failing dependency itself (the primary and failover database) emits no logs in this index; the deadlock, lock contention and connection-pool exhaustion are reported only from Company.Ops' point of view.
No Kubernetes objects for Company.Ops exist in the reachable cluster (only otel-demo/kind workloads), so pod status, restarts, events and container logs for these services could not be checked.
Jaeger service/operation listing and Prometheus label discovery returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run, so no trace or metric corroboration of error rate or latency is available.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether any configuration change accompanied the DR test could not be verified.

Several Elasticsearch searches over sub-windows (e.g. 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-04) returned INVALID_PARAMS without a reason; the content of those windows is therefore unread, although the full authorized-month query returned all 12 existing documents.
next_steps: Ask the DR test owner and the DBA team for the failover DB connection/lock metrics for 2026-11-23T11:14Z-16:14Z to confirm the deadlock and pool-exhaustion mechanism behind the job-creation 500.

Confirm which service the user's create-scheduled-job action actually hit (Company.Ops vs a separate WebJob host such as ops-prod-01/ops-prod-02) and re-test job creation now that the scheduler reports resumed operation at 16:14:02Z.
Check whether the read-only Prometheus proxy and Jaeger become reachable to corroborate error rates and latency for the .NET services during the DR window.
Forward these Company.Ops logs, particularly job-8831 at 14:14:02Z and job-8827 at 12:14:02Z, to the application owner as evidence for the post-DR review.

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
